target: PR #48 screenshot support in problem briefs
round_context: Mode: design review of the PR's approach, not a line-by-line diff review. PR #48 (branch worktree-fix-46-47-visuals, draft, closes issues #46 and #47) adds screenshot support to problem briefs. Deltas: (1) schema/problem-brief.schema.json — new diagram kind "image" (PNG/JPEG/WebP, required alt + caption, optional fileDark) and an optional "image" object on evidence items; (2) bin/validate-brief.mjs — checkImage() refuses missing/non-raster/>1 MB pictures when given a baseDir, warns above 6 MB total, and warns when a live entry's prose or evidence mentions .html/.png/.svg/mockup/screenshot and carries no image or svg; validateBrief gains a third baseDir parameter; (3) bin/render-brief.mjs — shot() embeds pictures as base64 data URIs inside a <button class="shot">, images grouped in a wrapping .shots row, a click toggles .zoom, dark/light swap by CSS; (4) bin/brief.mjs — --diagram list flag on raise and set (set appends to unwound.diagrams), validation now receives the brief's folder; (5) bin/extract-brief.mjs — writes embedded pictures back to files beside the recovered JSON, refusing paths that climb out of that folder; (6) SKILL.md, reference/entry-format.md, reference/diagrams.md, README.md — rule: show the reader what they must see; a path or markup line is not evidence for a visual question. Not done: no image resizing (zero-dependency scripts). Tests: 104 pass incl. 4 new. Zero-dependency Node 18+ project; no Python. No prior chorus record exists.

tldr: Five lenses found PR #48 delivers screenshots inside the page, but the recovery step that writes pictures back from a published page trusts that page too far, the phone tap does the opposite of the operator's ruling, and the visual-pointer warning guards wording instead of intent.

The top five fix extract first (refuse non-picture and dot-segment names, never overwrite, with a hostile-page test), then fit-to-screen tap with full-screen pinch-zoom, then replace the keyword warning with a per-evidence rule that intent to show must carry the picture.
Three 🔴 findings block merge: F1 (extract writes any file a page names), F8 (extract silently overwrites existing pictures) and F15 (no test fails if the folder-escape refusal is removed).

questions.question: Which quality matters most for problem-brief: (a) the operator can answer an entry from the published page alone, often on a phone; (b) the brief's JSON can be rebuilt from its published page; (c) zero dependencies and portable scripts; (d) the JSON stays readable and diffable?
questions.answer: Readable page first: (a) page answerable on a phone > (b) recovery > (c) zero dependencies > (d) diffable JSON.

questions.question: Who should the reviewers judge problem-brief as being built for: one operator, or public users through install.sh?
questions.answer: Public users: a tool shipped publicly through install.sh, used by people other than the author.

questions.question: On a phone, when you tap a screenshot in a brief, what should happen? The PR shows it at true pixel size with sideways scrolling.
questions.answer: Fit, pinch to zoom: keep it fitted to the screen width; open it fitted in a full-screen view where you pinch to zoom.

questions.question: Should an evidence screenshot have its own required caption, as issue #47 asked? The PR uses the evidence note as the caption.
questions.answer: Note is caption: keep the PR's choice; the evidence note already says what the picture shows.

questions.question: Does a typical session have any way to resize an image before the 1 MB refusal?
How often do live entries mention 'screenshot' or '.png' with no visual question behind them?
Does the artifact frame let the click toggle and the page's horizontal scroll work on a phone?
Is refusing a bad screenshot at validation while degrading a bad svg/archify drawing to a note at render time a deliberate split?
Is the data-brief-file markup that extract-brief parses a stable contract between render and extract, or an internal detail?
Does the project expect test-first, or only that a test lands with the change?
Is git show HEAD the intended scope, given local main is behind the PR's parent?
Issue #47 asked for a warning when the rendered page passes 8 MB; the PR warns when raw image bytes pass 6 MB. Was that change deliberate?

interview.degradation: Eight non-gate questions were deferred. Findings that depend on them state their assumption: no resizing tool exists in a session; the keyword warning's false-positive rate is unknown; phone behaviour in the artifact frame is read from CSS, not run; the refuse-versus-degrade split and the render-extract markup coupling are judged on the code alone; tests are expected to land with the change; scope is the PR's single commit; the 6 MB raw threshold is judged as written.

conflicts.disputed: Is the 1 MB per-picture cap a real obstacle? Richards (F3, now 🟢): this machine can resize, so the cap is reachable. Cooper (F5, 🟡): the author meets a hard stop whose hint names no tool, and the operator's question is never raised. Outcome differs: a refusal the author can act on, or a stop with no way forward.

Same cap, Norman's side. Richards (F3, now 🟢): resizing tools exist here. Norman (F12, 🟡): the refusal hint tells the author to resize, which public users may not be able to do, and leaves out retaking the shot narrower or cropped. Outcome differs: whether the message leads the author to a fix.

Where should the picture rule live? Richards (F4): keep render and extract copies of the img markup, pinned by the round-trip test. Uncle Bob (R2-4, F16): one function that validate, render and extract all call. No direct user-visible change; it sets how likely a later edit silently breaks recovering pictures.

Same question, Beck's side. Richards (F4): two copies are a sanctioned divergence, since extract importing the renderer would run its CLI. Beck (F21): the picture tag is one rule written twice; move it in a structure-only commit first. No direct user-visible change.

top_five.pull_quote: Extract trusts a stranger's page to name files, and the picture-type rule never reaches it; I got it to write .claude/settings.json.
top_five.value: Closes the only attacker-reachable write: a page someone else published can no longer name a non-picture file (e.g. .claude/settings.json) for extract to write. Unblocks merge (🔴).

top_five.pull_quote: The one line that stops a stranger's page from writing outside the folder has no test that fails without it.
top_five.value: Pins the F1 fix with a test that goes red if the path and type refusals are removed, so the guard cannot silently regress. Unblocks merge (🔴).

top_five.pull_quote: Recovering a brief from a page can quietly overwrite the screenshots already sitting in your folder, and nothing tells you it happened.
top_five.value: Stops recovery from silently overwriting screenshots already beside the JSON; the operator's own files are never lost to a page. Unblocks merge (🔴).

top_five.pull_quote: On a phone, tapping a screenshot to see it better makes it worse: a wide picture you scroll sideways through a narrow slot, the opposite of what the operator ruled.
top_five.value: Delivers the operator's ruling on the top-ranked quality: on a phone a tapped screenshot opens fitted in a full-screen view with pinch-zoom, instead of a true-size strip scrolled sideways.

top_five.pull_quote: Ask the entry whether the reader must see something, then require the picture; guessing from words both misses the #46 case and nags ordinary briefs.
top_five.value: Replaces the wording heuristic with the operator's rule (intent to show must carry the representation): fewer false warnings for public users, and the #46 case is caught per evidence item, not silenced by an unrelated svg.

reasons.reason: Choosing which recovery contract counts as stable is architecture. My lens sees only the consequence, pictures silently lost on recovery, and that is covered by R2-1.
